judged.rule: A subtle persistent top-center disclaimer ('Eksperimen pikiran. Angka dari model.' or equivalent) stays visible throughout the simulation.

The opening 4.5 seconds declare an identical twin-world simulation, name the single differing variable (topic + overview), and end on a which-world-is-better comparison question, over an active 3D diorama with a bold headline.
Two comparable twin worlds (World A vs World B) are established in a 50/50 horizontal split-screen with matching control variables before isolating one change.
The narrative shows an unexpected short-term friction or dip (around 20–45% of runtime) before revealing the deeper causal mechanism.
The causal mechanism is shown through a concrete 3D spatial or physical cutaway/demonstration rather than abstract text alone.
At least one dark-navy HUD data card (crossover line chart or 100-world robustness grid) proves the inflection point or sensitivity check.
City architecture, vehicles, and props use matte low-poly 3D assets (Polyfork kits or matching low-poly geometry) paired with readable procedural capsule characters.
Episodes query Polyfork MCP for topic-specific hero locations and props instead of lazily recycling only the 6 starter street models bundled in the board.
In split-screen beats focused on one world, the inactive half dims cleanly so the viewer's eye locks onto the active world.
Captions sit in the fixed lower band (y 1380–1580) in rounded bold white with thick dark-navy outline and warm-yellow active-word highlight.
The narration closes on a choice question that weaves the account name in naturally with 'dua dunia' kept consecutive; no spoken follow, subscribe, or like prompts appear.
The policy scenario, numbers, and dialogue are original and do not retell the reference episode.
